label_ok: yes: ZFS-only read failures across sanity, sanity-dom, sanity-flr, sanity-hsm, sanity-pcc, sanityn on this patchset; OST log shows ofd_lvbo_holes_detect failing SEEK_END with rc=-6 on ZFS
reasoning: The patch flips HOLE_DETECT_DEFAULT from none to all, so every client read/lock now asks the OST for hole extents. On osd-zfs, ofd_lvbo_holes_detect gets ENXIO from SEEK_END/SEEK_DATA on an empty or sparse object, the lock enqueue fails rc=-6 and the read fails; sanity-flr test_0d's lfsck_verify_pfid cat of an empty mirrored file is one such read. A reviewer reading 'enable hole detection by default' should know hole detection is served by backend SEEK_HOLE/SEEK_DATA semantics, which differ between ldiskfs and ZFS, and so ask for ZFS sessions; no path rule fires since the files are client osc/llite and obd.h.
catching_config_matters: zfs only (zfs-dne and zfs); predictable by reading (feature default enabling a backend-dependent server path), not by path
notes: The script is incidental: any read-heavy suite in ZFS fails (sanity 161d/247a in zfs-dne is bug 0). Selecting sanity in zfs-dne would catch the root cause; sanity-flr specifically is a per-script split. Candidate LLM-stage heuristic: a patch that changes a feature default or tunable that is implemented in the OSD/OFD needs both backends. Root cause is in already-merged ofd_lvb.c hole detection not handling ZFS ENXIO.

catching_config_matters: zfs only (ldiskfs custom passed 60a-60i); predictable from the diff: hole/punch-dependent EC behaviour is a known ldiskfs vs ZFS difference

label_ok: yes: sanity 64k is the test this patch adds, and it failed with the same 'interval stays 1200, want 30' signature on ps16 to ps22

In ps22 only the Ubuntu 24.04 client session failed, but earlier patchsets failed the same way on RHEL 10.0 and 10.1 clients in review-ldiskfs and review-dne-part-1, and ps22's own RHEL 10.1 and 9.7 DNE runs passed. sanity was already selected in ldiskfs-dne (edited script and client-rpc rule) for the right reason; the failure is a timing race in the init, not a configuration the patch points to.

label_ok: yes, but narrow: the new test_258 is not repeat-safe; it is the patch's test, not a defect in the lnet code change
reasoning: The patch replaces lnet_peer_discovery_disabled with an lnet_peer_discovery_mode enum and adds sanity-lnet test_258 to check the two parameters stay reconciled. In both subtest-change sessions (ldiskfs and zfs) the first iteration of test_258 passed; by the end of that iteration the framework had remounted the whole filesystem, so the repeat-2 iteration's reinit_dlc ran 'lnetctl lnet unconfigure' with Lustre mounted and got EBUSY ('lnetctl lnet unconfigure failed 240'). catching_config_matters: no: fails identically in ldiskfs and zfs subtest-change sessions; what matters is ONLY_REPEAT mode, not the configuration

Root cause: test_258 calls reinit_dlc without first doing cleanupall, unlike the router tests, so it only works when Lustre is already unmounted at test start.

label_ok: yes: this server patch breaks replay (replay-single, replay-dual, replay-vbr, recovery-small 145 all fail 3/3 on it and on its child 67604)
reasoning: The patch puts the md_op_spec bitfields (no_create, sp_cr_lookup, sp_rm_entry, sp_permitted, sp_replay, new sp_append_layout) inside a union with an unsigned int __sp_reset; in a union every bitfield member starts at bit 0, so they all alias one bit and setting sp_append_layout or sp_replay flips no_create and the rest, which breaks open/create replay. replay-single test_48 fails over the MDS after createmany; in single-MDT ZFS the breakage shows as 'client_up failed', while in DNE the same test fails later at unlinkmany (bug 4) and many other replay-single tests fail 3/3. The predictor ran replay-single in ldiskfs-dne and zfs-dne via the mds rule and caught the root bug; this unit is the same bug with a different message in a configuration (zfs single MDT) we did not request.
